rules.says: __PRESENT__ is selected without its twin __ABSENT__: the two cover one rule by different means; select both.
__PRESENT__ judge the same commands from one shared table: keep one, or a command is judged twice.
__PRESENT__ refuses every new dependency until __FILE__ exists (not found in the current directory); create it first.
__PRESENT__ refuses every MCP server until __FILE__ exists (not found in the current directory); create it first.
__PRESENT__ warns only, being measured (observe): nothing is refused.
__PRESENT__ is text only: nothing stops a violation (advisory).
__PRESENT__ is also in the chock plugin __PLUGIN__ (__PATH__): both copies fire; remove it from one of the two selections.
Codex skips a plugin's hooks until you review and trust them in /hooks, and asks again after a hook changes: until then every policy here is advisory.
Devin runs plugin hooks best-effort and fails open: a hook that errors or times out lets the action through.
This client names no file-write tool a hook can match, so a gate judges what a turn wrote only at turn end; the write itself is not held.
A gate judges the write before it lands in Copilot CLI (witnessed 2026-10-11, CLI 1.0.94 on Windows); in VS Code agent mode that is unmeasured.
On Cursor Teams and Enterprise an admin setting (Allow Local Plugin Imports) can turn local plugins off, and an installed marketplace plugin of the same name takes precedence over this one.
goose denies a PreToolUse call whose hook fails, because every entry sets on_failure: block; its Stop hooks stay fail-open, so a gate that fails at turn end lets the turn finish.

Grok's hooks fail open: a timeout, a crash or malformed output lets the action through, only an explicit deny blocks, and an allowManagedHooksOnly policy skips plugin hooks. No gate runs here: agentseam records neither a write-tool vocabulary nor a blocking Stop for grok.
Antigravity documents no fail mode for a hook and no plugin-root variable: the hooks name the plugin folder by absolute path, and a gate judges what a turn wrote only at turn end.
Evidence wanted: what you see goose do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/177
Evidence wanted: what you see Grok do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/188
Evidence wanted: what you see Antigravity do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/129

Gemini CLI treats a hook that exits with any code other than 0 or 2 as a warning and lets the call through, and Google is sunsetting Gemini CLI for consumer tiers in favor of Antigravity CLI (use the antigravity client there).

OpenHands documents no plugin-root variable: the hooks name the plugin folder by absolute path, and its hook runner blocks only on exit code 2 or a deny, so any other hook failure lets the call through.
Evidence wanted: what you see Gemini CLI do with this extension, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/132
Evidence wanted: what you see OpenHands do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/181
Untested: chock has not witnessed an install in this client. Its steps, its hooks and the plugin version string (<bundle.version>+<digest12>) are unmeasured there.
